2026-223.headline: City Adopts FY 2026-27 Supplemental Budget
2026-223.summary: Portland updated its 2026-27 budget to adjust city spending and manage financial risks to municipal services. The changes reallocate funds across city departments to help maintain existing public programs and services.
2026-223.title: Adopt a Supplemental Budget for FY 2026-27 to reduce potential risks to City services

2026-236.headline: Portland Leases Eastside Office for Safety Division
2026-236.summary: Portland's Community Safety Division is securing a new eastside office through a five-year lease with American Property Management. The agreement provides space for staff who coordinate local safety and emergency response programs. The move affects eastside residents accessing division services and city staff working in the area.
2026-236.title: *Authorize a five-year lease with American Property Management for Community Safety Division eastside office

2026-267.headline: City Pays $287,500 Settlement for Water Bureau Crash
2026-267.summary: The City of Portland will pay $287,500 to settle a lawsuit over a collision involving a Portland Water Bureau dump truck. The payment resolves claims made by an individual for bodily injuries suffered in the crash.
2026-267.title: *Pay settlement of Michael Duffer bodily injury lawsuit in the sum of $287,500 resulting from a collision with a City dump truck involving the Portland Water Bureau

2026-285.headline: City Seeks Partner to Develop Moda Center Land
2026-285.summary: Portland is beginning a search for a partner to build on city-owned land near the Moda Center. The city administrator will create a process to select a developer for these Rose Quarter properties. This move sets the stage for future construction and revitalization around the arena.
2026-285.title: Direct the City Administrator to advance a process to identify a development partner for City-owned properties adjacent to the Moda Center

2026-294.headline: City to Subsidize Transit Passes for Employees
2026-294.summary: A new pilot program will subsidize public transit passes for Portland city employees. Funding for the program comes from an increase of up to $245,000 in city bureau rates for the 2026-27 fiscal year. The decision affects municipal workers and city bureau budgets.
2026-294.title: *Authorize an increase up to $245,000 in bureau rates for FY 2026-27 to implement a pilot program to subsidize transit passes for City employees
